title: Be a paid campus ambassador for our trading app
scenario: A friendly senior student says their trading app pays a bonus for every classmate you sign up as a campus ambassador, and shows you a screenshot of their own quick profits.

answers.A: Sign up just to see how it works before recruiting anyone.
answers.B: Decline, and be cautious of any offer that pays more for recruiting people than for the product itself.
answers.C: Sign up and start recruiting classmates right away.

explanation: A program that rewards recruiting more than it rewards the underlying product is a hallmark of pyramid and affiliate-fraud schemes, regardless of who is presenting it.
proTip: If the real payout is recruiting people, the product is the excuse.
